answer: Sybil resistance comes from a superlinear stake curve, not a whitelist: any agent wanting grading seats must post collateral that grows faster than its seat share, and reward per extra seat thins toward the nadir as clones multiply. Five hundred sybil clones would each need the same velvet-edged bond as one honest agent, while seat 500 earns a fraction of seat one's opal fee. Cost to attacker is 500 locked stakes plus slashing on every verdict mismatch with the panel median; honest cost stays one bond.
